verdict.rationale: OpenCode's own GitHub integration runs tasks automatically when a GitHub comment mentions /opencode or /oc, and it sets up the workflow for you. That is one fixed event trigger, not a general system of user-defined event rules. The permission config only decides whether an action runs automatically, needs a prompt, or is blocked; that is an adjacent control, not event-triggered automation. Missing for 10: user-definable event→action rules or hooks, events beyond GitHub comment mentions, documentation of rule configuration, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Mention /opencode or /oc in your comment, and OpenCode will execute tasks within your GitHub Actions runner.
This will walk you through installing the GitHub app, creating the workflow, and setting up secrets.
